export interface UsePermalinkArgs {
    room?: Room;
    type?: PillType;
    url?: string;
}

export interface UsePermalinkResult {
    avatar: React.ReactElement | null;
    text: string | null;
    onClick: ((e: ButtonEvent) => void) | null;
    resourceId: string | null;
    type: PillType | "space" | null;

/**
 * Resolves a Matrix permalink (or explicit @room mention) into the data needed
 * to render a pill: effective type, raw resource id, human-friendly text,
 * an optional avatar element, and an optional user "view" click handler.
 *
 * When the input cannot be confidently resolved, the returned values lead
 * the consuming Pill component to render nothing (fail quiet).
 */
export function usePermalink({ room, type, url }: UsePermalinkArgs): UsePermalinkResult {
    return useMemo(() => {
        const client = MatrixClientPeg.get();

        // Explicit @room mention takes precedence over URL parsing
        if (type === PillType.AtRoomMention) {
            const roomId = room?.getId() ?? client.getUserId()?.replace(/^@/, "");
            return {
                avatar: room ? <RoomAvatar room={room} width={16} height={16} /> : null,
                text: "@room",
                onClick: null,
                resourceId: roomId,
                type: PillType.AtRoomMention,
            };
        }

        if (!url) {
            return { avatar: null, text: null, onClick: null, resourceId: null, type: null };
        }

        const permalink = parsePermalink(url);
        if (!permalink) {
            return { avatar: null, text: null, onClick: null, resourceId: null, type: null };
        }

        const entity = getPrimaryPermalinkEntity(permalink);
        if (!entity) {
            return { avatar: null, text: null, onClick: null, resourceId: null, type: null };
        }

        if (entity.type === "user") {
            const userId = entity.resourceId;
            const member = room?.getMember(userId);
            const displayName = member?.name || client.getProfileLookup(userId)?.displayName;
            return {
                avatar: member
                    ? <MemberAvatar member={member} width={16} height={16} />
                    : null,
                text: displayName || userId,
                onClick: member
                    ? (e: ButtonEvent) => {
                        dis.dispatch({
                            action: Action.ViewUser,
                            member,
                        });
                    }
                    : null,
                resourceId: userId,
                type: PillType.UserMention,
            };
        }

        if (entity.type === "room" || entity.type === "alias") {
            const roomIdOrAlias = entity.resourceId;
            const resolvedRoom =
                (roomIdOrAlias.startsWith("!") ? client.getRoom(roomIdOrAlias) : client.getRoomById(roomIdOrAlias)) ||
                (roomIdOrAlias.startsWith("#") ? client.getRoomById(roomIdOrAlias) : null);

            const isSpace = resolvedRoom?.isSpace() || client.isSpace(roomIdOrAlias);
            const roomName = resolvedRoom?.name || client.getRoom(roomIdOrAlias)?.name;

            return {
                avatar: resolvedRoom
                    ? <RoomAvatar room={resolvedRoom} width={16} height={16} />
                    : null,
                text: roomName || roomIdOrAlias,
                onClick: null,
                resourceId: roomIdOrAlias,
                type: isSpace ? "space" : PillType.RoomMention,
            };
        }

        return { avatar: null, text: null, onClick: null, resourceId: null, type: null };
    }, [room, type, url]);
}

    # email.policy.HTTP.

    public async skipTo(timeSeconds: number): Promise<void> {
        const timeMs = Math.round(timeSeconds * 1000);
        const targetEvent = this.chunkEvents.findByTime(timeMs);
        if (!targetEvent) return;

        const prevEvent = this.currentlyPlaying;
        if (prevEvent && prevEvent.getId() !== targetEvent.getId()) {
            this.playbacks.get(prevEvent.getId())?.stop();
        }

        const playback = await this.getPlaybackForEvent(targetEvent);
        const offsetMs = timeMs - this.chunkEvents.getLengthTo(targetEvent);
        await playback.skipTo(offsetMs / 1000);

            this.positionMs = timeMs;
            this.emit(VoiceBroadcastPlaybackEvent.PositionChanged, this.positionMs);
            this.liveData.update([this.timeSeconds, this.durationSeconds]);

        this.currentlyPlaying = targetEvent;

    private async getPlaybackForEvent(event: MatrixEvent): Promise<Playback> {
        const existing = this.playbacks.get(event.getId());
        if (existing) return existing;

        const helper = new MediaEventHelper(event);
        const blob = await helper.sourceBlob.value;
        const buffer = await blob.arrayBuffer();
        const playback = PlaybackManager.instance.createPlaybackInstance(buffer);
        await playback.prepare();
        playback.clockInfo.populatePlaceholdersFrom(event);
        this.playbacks.set(event.getId(), playback);

            if (this.currentlyPlaying?.getId() !== event.getId()) return;

                this.positionMs = newPositionMs;
                this.emit(VoiceBroadcastPlaybackEvent.PositionChanged, this.positionMs);
                this.liveData.update([this.timeSeconds, this.durationSeconds]);
            }
        });

export class VoiceBroadcastChunkEvents {
    private events: MatrixEvent[] = [];

    public getEvents(): MatrixEvent[] {
        return [...this.events];
    }

    public getNext(event: MatrixEvent): MatrixEvent | undefined {
        return this.events[this.events.indexOf(event) + 1];
    }

    public addEvent(event: MatrixEvent): void {
        if (this.addOrReplaceEvent(event)) {
            this.sort();
        }
    }

    public addEvents(events: MatrixEvent[]): void {
        const atLeastOneNew = events.reduce((newSoFar: boolean, event: MatrixEvent): boolean => {
            return this.addOrReplaceEvent(event) || newSoFar;
        }, false);

        if (atLeastOneNew) {
            this.sort();
        }
    }

    public includes(event: MatrixEvent): boolean {
        return !!this.events.find(e => e.getId() === event.getId());
    }

    public getLength(): number {
        return this.events.reduce((length: number, event: MatrixEvent) => {
            return length + this.calculateChunkLength(event);
        }, 0);
    }

    /**
     * Returns the cumulative length (in milliseconds) up to but not including the given event.
     */
    public getLengthTo(event: MatrixEvent): number {
        const index = this.events.indexOf(event);
        if (index === -1) {
            return 0;
        }
        let length = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < index; i++) {
            length += this.calculateChunkLength(this.events[i]);
        }
        return length;
    }

    /**
     * Finds the first chunk whose cumulative length (including itself) is >= time.
     */
    public findByTime(time: number): MatrixEvent | null {
        let cumulative = 0;
        for (const event of this.events) {
            cumulative += this.calculateChunkLength(event);
            if (cumulative >= time) {
                return event;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    private calculateChunkLength(event: MatrixEvent): number {
        return event.getContent()?.["org.matrix.msc1767.audio"]?.duration
            || event.getContent()?.info?.duration
            || 0;
    }

    private addOrReplaceEvent = (event: MatrixEvent): boolean => {
        this.events = this.events.filter(e => e.getId() !== event.getId());
        this.events.push(event);
        return true;
    };

    /**
     * Sort by sequence, if available for all events.
     * Else fall back to timestamp.
     */
    private sort(): void {
        const compareFn = this.allHaveSequence() ? this.compareBySequence : this.compareByTimestamp;
        this.events.sort(compareFn);
    }

    private compareBySequence = (a: MatrixEvent, b: MatrixEvent): number => {
        const aSequence = a.getContent()?.[VoiceBroadcastChunkEventType]?.sequence || 0;
        const bSequence = b.getContent()?.[VoiceBroadcastChunkEventType]?.sequence || 0;
        return aSequence - bSequence;
    };

    private compareByTimestamp = (a: MatrixEvent, b: MatrixEvent): number => {
        return a.getTs() - b.getTs();
    };

    private allHaveSequence(): boolean {
        return !this.events.some((event: MatrixEvent) => {
            const sequence = event.getContent()?.[VoiceBroadcastChunkEventType]?.sequence;
            return parseInt(sequence, 10) !== sequence;
        });
    }

        (state: VoiceBroadcastPlaybackState, _playback: VoiceBroadcastPlayback) => {

    );

    const [playbackInfoState, setPlaybackInfoState] = useState(playback.getInfoState());
    useTypedEventEmitter(
        playback,
        VoiceBroadcastPlaybackEvent.InfoStateChanged,
        (state: VoiceBroadcastInfoState) => {
            setPlaybackInfoState(state);
        },
    );

    const [duration, setDuration] = useState(playback.durationSeconds);
    useTypedEventEmitter(
        playback,
        VoiceBroadcastPlaybackEvent.LengthChanged,
        durationMs => setDuration(durationMs / 1000),
    );

    return {
        duration,
        live: playbackInfoState !== VoiceBroadcastInfoState.Stopped,
        room: room,
        sender: playback.infoEvent.sender,
        toggle: playbackToggle,
        playbackState,
    };
};

+.. _platform_eric_eccli:
+
+Ericsson ECCLI
+================
+
+.. contents::
+   :local:
+   :depth: 2
+
+Introduction
+-------------
+
+This guide describes how to use Ansible Network with Ericsson ECCLI devices.
+
+Connection options
+------------------
+
+The following connection options are available for Ericsson ECCLI devices:
+
+.. list-table:: Connection options
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Option
+     - Value
+     - Description
+   * - ``host``
+     - (required)
+     - The hostname of the device.
+   * - ``port``
+     - (optional)
+     - The TCP port to connect to on the device.
+   * - ``username``
+     - (optional)
+     - The username used for authentication.
+   * - ``password``
+     - (optional)
+     - The password used for authentication.
+   * - ``ssh_keyfile``
+     - (optional)
+     - The path to the SSH private key used for authentication.
+   * - ``ssh_password``
+     - (optional)
+     - The password for the SSH private key.
+   * - ``network_os``
+     - ``eric_eccli``
+     - The value of the ``network_os`` inventory variable for this platform.
+
+Using the network_cli connection
+--------------------------------
+
+To connect to an Ericsson ECCLI device, use the ``network_cli`` connection
+type and set ``network_os`` to ``eric_eccli``.
+
+Example inventory
+-----------------
+
+.. code-block:: ini
+
+   [eccli]
+   eccli1 ansible_host=192.0.2.10
+
+   [eccli:vars]
+   ansible_connection=network_cli
+   ansible_network_os=eric_eccli
+   ansible_user=admin
+   ansible_password=secret
+
+Example playbook
+----------------
+
+.. code-block:: yaml
+
+   - name: Run commands on Ericsson ECCLI
+     hosts: eccli
+     gather_facts: false
+     tasks:
+       - name: Run a list of commands
+         eric_eccli_command:
+           commands:
+             - show version
+             - show interface status
+           wait_for:
+             - "stdout.0 contains 'ECCLI'"
+           match: all
+           retries: 10
+           interval: 1
+
+       - name: Show the output
+         debug:
+           var: result.stdout
+
+See Also
+---------
+
+* :ref:`Ansible Network User Guide <network_user_guide>`
+* :ref:`Ansible Network Platform Index <platform_index>`

+.. _platform_eric_eccli:
+
+Ericsson ECCLI
+================
+
+.. contents::
+   :local:
+   :depth: 2
+
+Introduction
+-------------
+
+This guide describes how to use Ansible Network with Ericsson ECCLI devices.
+
+Connection options
+------------------
+
+The following connection options are available for Ericsson ECCLI devices:
+
+.. list-table:: Connection options
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Option
+     - Value
+     - Description
+   * - ``host``
+     - (required)
+     - The hostname of the device.
+   * - ``port``
+     - (optional)
+     - The TCP port to connect to on the device.
+   * - ``username``
+     - (optional)
+     - The username used for authentication.
+   * - ``password``
+     - (optional)
+     - The password used for authentication.
+   * - ``ssh_keyfile``
+     - (optional)
+     - The path to the SSH private key used for authentication.
+   * - ``ssh_password``
+     - (optional)
+     - The password for the SSH private key.
+   * - ``network_os``
+     - ``eric_eccli``
+     - The value of the ``network_os`` inventory variable for this platform.
+
+Using the network_cli connection
+--------------------------------
+
+To connect to an Ericsson ECCLI device, use the ``network_cli`` connection
+type and set ``network_os`` to ``eric_eccli``.
+
+Example inventory
+-----------------
+
+.. code-block:: ini
+
+   [eccli]
+   eccli1 ansible_host=192.0.2.10
+
+   [eccli:vars]
+   ansible_connection=network_cli
+   ansible_network_os=eric_eccli
+   ansible_user=admin
+   ansible_password=secret
+
+Example playbook
+----------------
+
+.. code-block:: yaml
+
+   - name: Run commands on Ericsson ECCLI
+     hosts: eccli
+     gather_facts: false
+     tasks:
+       - name: Run a list of commands
+         eric_eccli_command:
+           commands:
+             - show version
+             - show interface status
+           wait_for:
+             - "stdout.0 contains 'ECCLI'"
+           match: all
+           retries: 10
+           interval: 1
+
+       - name: Show the output
+         debug:
+           var: result.stdout
+
+See Also
+---------
+
+* :ref:`Ansible Network User Guide <network_user_guide>`
+* :ref:`Ansible Network Platform Index <platform_index>`

+
+.. contents::

+
+Introduction
+-------------
+
+This guide describes how to use Ansible Network with Ericsson ECCLI devices.
+
+Connection options
+------------------
+
+The following connection options are available for Ericsson ECCLI devices:
+
+.. list-table:: Connection options
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Option
+     - Value
+     - Description
+   * - ``host``
+     - (required)
+     - The hostname of the device.
+   * - ``port``
+     - (optional)
+     - The TCP port to connect to on the device.

+     - (optional)
+     - The username used for authentication.
+   * - ``password``
+     - (optional)
+     - The password used for authentication.

+     - (optional)
+     - The path to the SSH private key used for authentication.

+     - (optional)
+     - The password for the SSH private key.
+   * - ``network_os``
+     - ``eric_eccli``
+     - The value of the ``network_os`` inventory variable for this platform.

+Using the network_cli connection
+--------------------------------
+
+To connect to an Ericsson ECCLI device, use the ``network_cli`` connection

+

+* :ref:`Ansible Network Platform Index <platform_index>`

+      - all
+      - any
+    default: all
+  retries:
+    description: Number of times to retry running the commands.
+    type: int
+    default: 10
+  interval:
+    description: Seconds to wait between retries.
+    type: int
+    default: 1
+author:

+"""

+EXAMPLES = """
+- name: Run commands on an Ericsson ECCLI device
+  eric_eccli_command:
+    commands:
+      - show version
+      - show interfaces
+    wait_for:
+      - "show version contains 12.3"
+    match: all
+    retries: 5
+    interval: 2
+"""
+
+RETURN = """
+stdout:
+  description: The output of each command, one entry per command.
+  type: list
+  returned: always
+  sample: ["12.3.4", "eth0: up"]
+warnings:
+  description: Warnings collected during execution, e.g. skipped config commands in check mode.
+  type: list
+  returned: when warnings are generated
+  sample: ["only non-config commands are supported when using check mode, not executing configure terminal"]
+"""
+
+
+def parse_commands(module, warnings):
+    """
+    Normalize the module's commands and, in check mode, skip config commands.
+
+    :param module: The AnsibleModule instance
+    :param warnings: A list that receives a warning for each skipped config command
+    :return: The list of commands to actually execute
+    """
+    commands = module.params['commands']
+    normalized = []
+    for command in commands:
+        if module.check_mode and command.startswith('conf'):
+            warnings.append(
+                'only non-config commands are supported when using check mode, not executing %s' % command
+            )
+        else:
+            normalized.append(command)
+    return normalized

+def _build_conditionals(module, outputs):
+    """
+    Build the list of (condition_met, condition_text) pairs for the wait_for conditions.
+    """
+    wait_for = module.params['wait_for']
+    conditionals = []
+    for condition in wait_for:
+        # Support "contains <text>" and "matches <regex>" style conditions.
+        met = False
+        if ' contains ' in condition:
+            _, text = condition.split(' contains ', 1)
+            for output in outputs:
+                if text in output:
+                    met = True
+                    break
+        elif ' matches ' in condition:
+            import re
+            _, pattern = condition.split(' matches ', 1)
+            for output in outputs:
+                if re.search(pattern, output):
+                    met = True
+                    break
+        else:
+            # Treat the whole condition as a plain substring match.
+            for output in outputs:
+                if condition in output:
+                    met = True
+                    break
+        conditionals.append((met, condition))
+    return conditionals
+
+
+def main():
+    """Entry point for the eric_eccli_command module."""
+    module = AnsibleModule(
+        argument_spec=dict(
+            commands=dict(type='list', elements='str', required=True),
+            wait_for=dict(type='list', elements='str', default=[], aliases=['waitfor']),
+            match=dict(type='str', choices=['all', 'any'], default='all'),
+            retries=dict(type='int', default=10),
+            interval=dict(type='int', default=1),
+        ),
+        supports_check_mode=True,
+    )
+
+    warnings = []
+    commands = parse_commands(module, warnings)
+
+    retries = module.params['retries']
+    interval = module.params['interval']
+    match = module.params['match']
+    wait_for = module.params['wait_for']
+
+    outputs = []
+    conditionals = []
+    for attempt in range(1, retries + 1):
+        outputs = run_commands(module, commands)
+        if wait_for:
+            conditionals = _build_conditionals(module, outputs)
+            if match == 'all':
+                satisfied = all(met for met, _ in conditionals)
+            else:
+                satisfied = any(met for met, _ in conditionals)
+            if satisfied:
+                break
+        else:
+            break
+        if attempt < retries:
+            sleep(interval)
+
+    if wait_for and not (match == 'all' and all(met for met, _ in conditionals) or match == 'any' and any(met for met, _ in conditionals)):
+        unmet = [text for met, text in conditionals if not met]
+        module.fail_json(
+            msg='All of the wait_for conditions were not satisfied after %d attempts' % retries,
+            unmet_conditions=unmet,
+            stdout=outputs,
+            warnings=warnings,
+        )
+
+    module.exit_json(
+        changed=False,
+        stdout=outputs,
+        warnings=warnings,
+    )

        return val

    rec: dict,

    """
    Adds a new Edition to Open Library, or overwrites existing_edition with rec data.

    The overwrite option exists for cases where the existing edition data
    should be (nearly) completely overwritten by rec data. Revision 1 promise
    items are an example.

    Checks for existing Works.
    Creates a new Work, and Author, if required,
    otherwise associates the new Edition with the existing Work.

    :param dict rec: Edition record to add (no further checks at this point)
    :rtype: dict
    :return:
        {
            "success": False,
            "error": <error msg>
        }
      OR
        {
            "success": True,
            "work": {"key": <key>, "status": "created" | "modified" | "matched"},
            "edition": {"key": <key>, "status": "created"},
            "authors": [{"status": "matched", "name": "John Smith", "key": <key>}, ...]
        }
    """

    try:
        # get an OL style edition dict
        rec_as_edition = import_record_to_edition(rec)
        edition: dict[str, Any]
        if existing_edition:

            # now, because we'll really only come here when overwriting a promise
            # item
            edition = existing_edition.dict() | rec_as_edition

            # Preserve source_records to avoid data loss.
            edition['source_records'] = existing_edition.get(
                'source_records', []
            ) + rec.get('source_records', [])

            # Preserve existing authors, if any.
            if authors := existing_edition.get('authors'):
                edition['authors'] = authors

        else:
            edition = rec_as_edition

    except InvalidLanguage as e:
        return {
            'success': False,
            'error': str(e),
        }

    if not (edition_key := edition.get('key')):
        edition_key = web.ctx.site.new_key('/type/edition')

    cover_url = edition.pop('cover', None)
    if cover_url and not check_cover_url_host(cover_url):
        cover_url = None

    cover_id = None
    if cover_url:
        cover_id = add_cover(cover_url, edition_key, account_key=account_key)
    if cover_id:
        edition['covers'] = [cover_id]

    edits: list[dict] = []  # Things (Edition, Work, Authors) to be saved
    reply = {}
    # edition.authors may have already been processed by import_authors() in build_query(),
    # but not necessarily
    author_in = [

            author_import_record_to_author(a, eastern=east_in_by_statement(rec, a))
            if isinstance(a, dict)
            else a
        )
        for a in edition.get('authors', [])
    ]
    # build_author_reply() adds authors to edits
    (authors, author_reply) = build_author_reply(
        author_in, edits, rec['source_records'][0]
    )

    if authors:
        edition['authors'] = authors
        reply['authors'] = author_reply

    work_key = safeget(lambda: edition['works'][0]['key'])
    work_state = 'created'
    # Look for an existing work
    if not work_key and 'authors' in edition:
        work_key = find_matching_work(edition)
    if work_key:
        work = web.ctx.site.get(work_key)
        work_state = 'matched'
        need_update = False
        for k in subject_fields:
            if k not in rec:
                continue
            for s in rec[k]:
                if normalize(s) not in [
                    normalize(existing) for existing in work.get(k, [])
                ]:

                    need_update = True
        if cover_id:
            work.setdefault('covers', []).append(cover_id)
            need_update = True
        if need_update:
            work_state = 'modified'
            edits.append(work.dict())
    else:
        # Create new work
        work = new_work(edition, rec, cover_id)
        work_state = 'created'
        work_key = work['key']
        edits.append(work)

    assert work_key

    edition['key'] = edition_key
    edits.append(edition)

    # archive.org item after successful import:

def author_import_record_to_author(author_import_record: dict[str, Any], eastern=False) -> "Author | dict[str, Any]":
    """

        'death_date',
